rationale: Section 8.2.1(a)(i)(B) sets a two-working-day acknowledgment deadline for complaints made by email.
Section 8.2.1(a)(ii) requires seeking resolution on first contact where possible; urgency does not remove that duty when first-contact resolution is possible.

Section 8.2.1(a)(viii) requires implementation of the urgent aspects within two working days after receipt if the consumer accepts the proposed resolution. The situation does not establish acceptance, so this implementation obligation is not entailed or negated.

Section 8.2.1(a)(iv)(B) requires remedy tailoring to individual circumstances where those circumstances have been advised to the supplier. No such circumstances have been advised in the situation; the specific duty is not established by this provision.
Section 8.2.1(a)(iv)(C) requires addressing the root cause of a wider issue indicated by complaints.
Section 8.2.1(a)(iv)(D) requires resolving billing errors in current bills even where complaints also reveal a wider problem addressed by 8.2.1(a)(iv)(C).

Section 8.2.1(a)(v) restricts credit management action for a specified disputed amount while the complaint remains unresolved to the consumer’s satisfaction and is being investigated. Those triggering circumstances do not hold in the situation; neither the continuing prohibition nor its negation follows from this provision.

Section 8.2.1(a)(vi) requires delaying commencement of legal proceedings while the complaint is being handled internally and for seven working days following outcome notification. Both specified periods have ended; the provision does not establish a continuing duty or its negation.
Section 8.2.1(a)(ix)(A) requires advising the consumer of the reasons for anticipated delay before working day 15 when ordinary complaint resolution is expected to exceed 15 working days.

Section 8.2.1(a)(ix)(C) requires external-dispute-resolution advice when the anticipated delay is a further ten working days or more and is not due to a declared mass service disruption. The situation establishes neither the additional delay length nor the disruption condition, leaving the obligation underdetermined.
Section 8.2.1(a)(viii) requires implementing the accepted urgent aspects within two working days after complaint receipt; the scenario specifies same-day acceptance.
Section 8.2.1(a)(ix)(C) requires external-dispute-resolution advice for the specified further delay absent a declared mass service disruption.
Section 8.2.1(a)(x) requires advising consumers of delays to promised timeframes; continuing to work toward resolution does not eliminate that notice duty.
Section 8.2.1(a)(xi) requires a means for consumers or former customers to monitor complaint progress.

Section 8.2.1(a)(xii) requires advising the consumer of the complaint's resolution in everyday language as soon as practicable after investigation; everyday language is a required manner of communication.

Section 8.2.1(a)(xiii) specifies a default ten-working-day implementation deadline unless the parties agree otherwise or outstanding consumer action prevents completion. An alternative timeframe was agreed without specifying its length, so the default ten-day obligation is not established or negated.
Section 8.2.1(a)(xiv) permits closure only with consent or compliance with an enumerated exception.
Section 8.2.1(a)(xv) requires written confirmation within five working days when a complaint is closed with consent and the consumer requests it.
Section 8.2.1(b) requires notice about internal prioritisation and escalation upon dissatisfaction with timeframes or a request for urgency.

Section 8.2.1(c) requires information about both internal escalation and external dispute resolution options, including the TIO; providing the former does not remove the obligation to provide the latter.
